To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) the random graph G(n,p) is a persistent Markov chain and (b) the random search tree T(n,k) is a persistent random walk.

the random variables associated with the first few input values of a sequential algorithm are often sufficient to predict the asymptotic behavior of the algorithm, and that this can be established by using techniques of discrete potential theory.

the following two properties hold for a broad class of random discrete structures: (1) the first few random input values can have a significant influence on the long term behavior of the Markov chain, (2) the long term behavior can be described in terms of the discrete potential theory of the Markov transition matrix.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of algorithms that generate discrete structures, such as graphs or search trees, from random input.

the study of the persistence of randomness in discrete stochastic systems and the development of new techniques to analyze such systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the random graph theory of Erdös and Rényi, and the theory of random search trees of Knuth, have been extended to the case of random inputs.
the persistence of randomness is a very useful concept for the analysis of random algorithms.
the persistence of randomness in randomly growing structures can be detected and analyzed by methods of discrete potential theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the discrete potential theory provides a useful tool to detect and quantify long term dependence in random processes generated by a sequential process.

, in the presence of randomness, a random input sequence can be used to generate random discrete structures whose long term behavior depends on the first few input values, but not on the entire sequence.
the persistence of randomness can often be detected and quantitatively measured with techniques from discrete Markov chains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a random graph process is not necessarily well approximated by a random graph model if the latter does not take the persistence of randomness into account.
the Markov chain generated by a sequential randomised algorithm can be analysed by studying the potential theoretic properties of the underlying discrete structure.
the discrete structures generated by random input can exhibit long term memory, and that this memory can be quantified using potential theoretic techniques.
